name: Multi-Factor Authentication Enforcement Configuration
description: Export of the identity provider's authentication policy showing which factors are enforced, which user populations and applications the policy applies to, and every exclusion from it.

expected_content.element: Policy definition showing the required authentication factors
expected_content.why: Establishes what the control actually enforces, as distinct from what the policy document says.

expected_content.element: Assignment scope: user groups, applications, and network conditions the policy applies to
expected_content.why: Coverage is the substance of this control; a policy applied to a subset is a design deficiency.

expected_content.element: Complete list of exclusions, exceptions, and bypass conditions
expected_content.why: Exclusions are where this control usually fails. Their absence from the export is itself a red flag.

expected_content.element: Enumeration of authentication paths not governed by the identity provider (direct logins, VPN, SSH/bastion, cloud CLI, long-lived API tokens, vendor admin portals)
expected_content.why: Uncovered paths defeat the control regardless of how strong the governed path is.

expected_content.element: Tenant or organization identifier and export timestamp
expected_content.why: Attribution and dating; an undated configuration screenshot cannot be placed within the period.

expected_content.element: Configuration change history covering the examination period
expected_content.why: Required in practice for a Type 2 conclusion: point-in-time state alone cannot show the setting held throughout the period.

owner: IT / Identity and Access Management owner
source_system_examples: Identity provider conditional access policy export
Cloud provider IAM policy and account settings API
Infrastructure-as-code definition of the identity configuration

freshness_expectation.rationale: DriftGuard default for a continuously enforced configuration. Not an audit rule.

redaction_guidance: Never include enrolled factor secrets, recovery codes, seed values, or break-glass credentials.
Group and user names may be pseudonymised provided scope coverage remains demonstrable.
retention_guidance: Capture on a schedule and retain each dated snapshot; a series of snapshots is what converts point-in-time state into period coverage.

validation_rules.rule: A configuration export exists for the in-scope identity provider.
Every authentication path into the declared system boundary is either covered by the policy or listed as an exclusion with a compensating control.
The export is dated within the examination period, or within the DriftGuard freshness window for continuous monitoring.
For a Type 2 conclusion, the export is accompanied by configuration change history or repeated dated snapshots covering the period.
The artifact is an API or console export identifying the tenant, not an uncontextualised screenshot.

common_issues.issue: Policy enforced only for a pilot group or a single application while presented as environment-wide.
common_issues.impact: Coverage claimed in the system description exceeds coverage actually configured.

common_issues.issue: Break-glass and service accounts excluded with no compensating control and no alerting on use.
common_issues.impact: An unmonitored bypass exists around the control.

common_issues.issue: Long-lived API tokens or personal access tokens treated as out of scope.
common_issues.impact: A credential-only authentication path persists, defeating the control's objective.

common_issues.issue: Single undated screenshot offered as evidence for a twelve-month period.
common_issues.impact: Point-in-time state cannot support an operating-effectiveness conclusion.

source_refs.supports: The point-in-time versus period pairing expectation and the common issues list.
Freshness window and snapshot retention approach.

notes: Exercises the point_in_time period_coverage case. The Phase 1 gap is now closed: EV-CONFIG-001 supplies the configuration change history needed to convert point-in-time state into period coverage for a Type 2 conclusion.
Backfilled with evidence_role and origin in the CC6 phase (schema 0.2.0). Content otherwise unchanged.
